name: @tabnas/xml
description: XML 1.0 parsing for the tabnas engine, with namespaces and entities.

loss: An element tree, the one the reader builds, is written as it is: an object whose members are name, localName, attributes and children, with text and elements as children.

A plain tree, from another format or a program, is written through the embedding and read back by the same convention: the root value as the element document, an object as an element of type="object" whose members are member elements, each with a name attribute holding its key, and an array as an element of type="array" whose elements are item elements.

In the embedding a string is its element's text and an empty string an element of type="string" with no text; a number is its text in an element of type="number", INF, -INF or NaN where it is not finite; a boolean is true or false in an element of type="boolean"; and null is an element of type="null" with no text.

The XML declaration, the DOCTYPE, comments and processing instructions are not kept: an entity the DOCTYPE declared is written as its replacement text, and an attribute it defaulted is written on the element.

CDATA sections are not kept: their text is written as escaped character data, and two texts the reader read either side of a CDATA section, a comment or a processing instruction read back as one; an empty text child is written as an empty CDATA section, the one spelling that reads back as one.

Namespace prefixes are written as part of the name; localName, prefix, namespace, space and lang are not written, since a reader derives them again from the name and from the xmlns, xml:space and xml:lang attributes, which are kept.

Entity and character references are written as their characters, escaped where XML requires; a carriage return, and a tab or a line feed in an attribute's value, are written as character references, since a bare one is normalised away when read.
Attribute values are written double-quoted, and the quoting, the white space inside a tag and a byte order mark are not kept.
